title: Annotatio III §.I: MARPURGENSE — first of the more perfect Consociation attempts, though lowest grade (all dogmas but one; Luther refuses right hand of fraternity)
pass_a_gloss: This MARBURG one I would call the First of the more perfect Consociation efforts, though of the lowest Grade: more perfect, because the Consensus was with respect to all dogmas, one excepted; but of the lowest Grade, because Luther refused to give the right hand of Fraternity — Chytraeus p. 647.
pass_b_english: I would call this Marburg attempt the first of the more complete Consociation efforts — though still of the lowest grade.
More complete, because they agreed on every dogma but one; lowest grade, because Luther would not give the right hand of fraternity (Chytraeus, p. 647).
source_text: MARPURGENSE hoc, Primum perfectiorum Consociationis moliminum dixerim, etsi Gradûs infimi: Perfectiorum, quia Consensus fuit ratione omnium dogmatum, exceptô unô; At Infimi Gradus, quia dextram Fraternitatis Lutherus dare noluit Chyt. pag. 647.

lemmas.latin: MARPURGENSE hoc, Primum perfectiorum Consociationis moliminum
lemmas.gloss: this Marburg [attempt], the First of the more perfect Consociation efforts

lemmas.note: perfect in scope, low in fraternity outcome

lemmas.gloss: Luther refused to give the right hand of Fraternity

notes: Hexades Annotatio III §.I densify §200; Strimesius ranks Marburg first perfectior molimen, grade infimus.
